step_outcomes.description: Set up working copy + R env; load NEW7080.dta, rename per .do block, cross-tab CENSUS x cohort
step_outcomes.stdout: CENSUS 70 / 1920-1929 = 247199; CENSUS 80 / 1930-1939 = 329509; CENSUS 80 / 1940-1949 = 486926. Total 1063634 obs, 27 cols. AGEQ is an age (40-50) for 1970 census but a date (1930-1950) for 1980, confirming the AGEQ-1900 transform. QOB 1..4 populated.
step_outcomes.notes: Cross-tab matches expected three populated groups exactly. YOB is 4-digit (1920-1929) for the 1970 census and 2-digit (30-49) for the 1980 census; the .do YOB-dummy block handles both codings. CENSUS 80 count (816435) = 329509 + 486926 exactly, so the COHORT filter alone uniquely selects the right census/cohort without a separate CENSUS filter.

step_outcomes.description: Table III Wald estimates: group means (Q1 vs Q2-4) of ln wage and education, Wald ratio, bivariate OLS. Panel A=1970/1920-29, Panel B=1980/1930-39
step_outcomes.notes: Matches published Table III: Panel A Wald 0.0715 / OLS 0.0801; Panel B Wald 0.1020 / OLS 0.0709. Wald SE computed as SE(reduced-form wage diff)/|education diff| (standard AK Wald SE, denominator treated as first stage); group-diff SEs use unequal-variance (Welch) form. Both first-quarter groups have lower mean wage AND lower mean education than the 2nd-4th quarter group, exactly the AK pattern.

step_outcomes.description: Table I quarter-of-birth effects on educational outcomes (1980 Census, cohorts 1930-39 & 1940-49). MA(+2,-2) detrend of cohort-quarter means; LPM/OLS of detrended outcome on QTR1-3; joint F-test.
step_outcomes.stdout: total_education 1930-39: I=-0.119(0.017) II=-0.081(0.017) III=+0.001(0.017) F=25.06; 1940-49: I=-0.084 II=-0.027 III=-0.019 F=16.25. high_school_graduate 1930-39: I=-0.0188 F=44.0; 1940-49: I=-0.0141 F=45.9. college/masters/doctoral: quarter effects near zero (|coef|<=0.005). educ_for_hs_graduates: F=6.6/8.6.
step_outcomes.notes: Sign/scale checks all pass: Q1 coefficient negative for total education (-0.119, -0.084) and HS graduation (-0.019, -0.014) in BOTH cohorts; college/masters/doctoral quarter effects near zero (no seasonal pattern), though F is 'significant' purely from the huge N. total_education 1930-39 (I=-0.119, II=-0.081, F=25.06) closely matches the published Table I (approx -0.124, -0.086, F=25.1). Magnitudes approximate per the plan note: the shipped extract is the positive-earnings sample, which differs slightly from the paper's education-based Table I sample. Detrend done per cohort (each cohort's own 40-cell time series); boundary cells (first-2/last-2 quarters) dropped.

step_outcomes.description: Descriptive season-of-birth series behind Figures I, II, IV, V (1980 Census, born 1930-1949): cell means of EDUC and LWKLYWGE by (YOB,QOB), MA(+2,-2) detrend, Q1-dip count, age-earnings slopes.
step_outcomes.stdout: Figure IV: 18 of 19 birth-years have Q1 education below the MA(+2,-2) prediction. Age-earnings slope (mean lnwage on YOB): 1940-49 (younger)=-0.02424 (steep => wages rise with age over 30-39), 1930-39 (older)=-0.00068 (flat). Mean lnwage Q1=5.8364 vs Q2-4=5.8396 (Q1 earns 0.0032 less).
step_outcomes.notes: All qualitative patterns reproduced: recurring first-quarter education dip (18/19 birth-years below MA prediction); positively-sloped age-earnings profile for the younger 1940-49 cohort (|slope|=0.024) that flattens for the older 1930-39 cohort (0.0007); first-quarter births earn slightly less than surrounding births. Detrend for Figure IV done over the full continuous 1930-1949 chronology (80 cells). LIMITATION (per plan): the shipped extract spans only birth years 1930-1949, so the 1950-1959 secularly-declining panels of Figures III/IV are NOT reproducible from this data; only the 1930-1949 rising cohorts are covered.
